explanations.explanation: That’s it, baker. David says, "I shall not want," meaning he won’t lack a thing. With the LORD as his shepherd, he’s taken care of.
Not quite. David isn’t talking about earning—he’s talking about needing. The LORD provides, so he won’t lack.
Close, but not the word. David says he won’t lack anything he needs, not that he won’t lose anything.
You got it, baker. Green pastures and quiet waters? That’s the picture of rest and peace, like a sheep lying down in the best spot.
Not this one. Hard work doesn’t fit the scene. David’s painting a picture of rest, not effort.
Nope. Danger’s the last thing on David’s mind here. This is all about peace and safety.
Perfect bake! The LORD doesn’t just take care of David’s body—He restores his soul. That’s care that goes deep.
Not this time. David’s talking about renewal, not testing. The LORD restores his soul.
Nope. Weighing isn’t the word here. The LORD restores David’s soul, like fixing what’s broken.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His name
explanations.explanation: Box-worthy! David says the LORD guides him in the paths of righteousness for the sake of His name. It’s all about God’s glory.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His flock
explanations.explanation: Not quite. The reason David gives is for the sake of His name, not the flock.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His land
explanations.explanation: Nope. The text says it’s for the sake of His name, not His land.

explanations.answer: Because the LORD is with him
explanations.explanation: That’s a keeper! David says he won’t fear evil because the LORD is with him. Even in the darkest valley, he’s not alone.
Not this one. David’s strength isn’t the point. It’s the LORD’s presence that takes away the fear.
Nope. The length of the valley isn’t the reason. It’s the LORD’s presence that comforts him.
Baked just right. David says the LORD’s rod and staff comfort him. Even in the valley of the shadow of death, those tools bring comfort.
Still doughy. David says the rod and staff comfort him, so this one’s true.
Fine work, baker! The LORD prepares a table for David, like a host welcoming a guest. That’s a picture of care and honor.
Not this time. David’s talking about a table, not a tent. The LORD sets a table before him.
Nope. The word here is table. The LORD prepares a table, not a bed.
Came out burnt. David says the LORD prepares a table for him in the presence of his enemies, not far away from them.
That’s a keeper! The table is prepared in the presence of his enemies, so this one’s false.
Perfect bake! A cup that overflows means David has more than enough. The LORD’s blessings are abundant.
Nope. An overflowing cup isn’t about carelessness. It’s about abundance.
Not this one. The picture is of abundance, not haste. His cup overflows because he has more than enough.
Baked just right. David says goodness and mercy will follow him all the days of his life. That’s a promise of God’s constant care.
Not quite. David’s talking about goodness and mercy, not wealth and honor.
Nope. The text says goodness and mercy, not strength and wisdom.

explanations.answer: In the house of the LORD
explanations.explanation: Fine work, baker! David closes with the promise that he will dwell in the house of the LORD forever. That’s where he wants to be.
Not this one. David’s talking about the house of the LORD, not Hebron.
Nope. The text says the house of the LORD, not the land of Canaan.
